items.detail: Wall Street steadied on Friday: the S&P 500 edged up **0.05% to 7,412** and the Dow rebounded **0.46% to 51,947**, but the Nasdaq Composite slipped **0.64% to 24,976** for a mixed close that still left the index down a second straight week.
items.why: A sharp reversal in oil pulled the Dow and S&P off Thursday's lows, but a fresh semiconductor selloff kept the tech-heavy Nasdaq under water.

items.detail: Crude sharply reversed Thursday's spike above $100 — **Brent fell ~4% to $96.78** and **WTI dropped ~3% to $89.31** — though both still finished the week up 8–10%.
items.why: Reports that Pakistan, backed by China, is pushing to revive U.S.–Iran talks eased fears of a Strait of Hormuz disruption and cooled the Middle East supply premium.

items.detail: A memory-chip rout dragged tech lower: **SanDisk tumbled ~11%**, with **Micron and SK Hynix down ~6%** and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index off more than 3%, while **Intel fell ~6.5%** despite a quarterly beat.
items.why: A selloff in Korean memory names spilled into U.S. chipmakers as investors extended this week's worry over ballooning AI capital-spending costs.

items.detail: The **10-year Treasury yield eased to ~4.67%**, backing off Thursday's 4.707% high — the highest since January 2025.
items.why: The retreat in oil below $100 took some of the inflation heat out of the bond market, letting yields tick lower.

items.detail: The coming week is pivotal: the **FOMC meets July 28–29** with fed funds futures pricing a **~35% chance of a quarter-point hike**, followed by **Microsoft, Meta and Apple earnings** plus Q2 GDP and PCE data.
items.why: Traders are bracing for whether the oil-driven inflation impulse pushes the Fed toward tightening, even as Q2 S&P 500 earnings are tracking a ~38% year-over-year jump per FactSet.

items.detail: Indian equities closed the week limping through a **fifth straight losing session**, with the Nifty 50 at **23,767.45** and the Sensex at **76,059.77**, but the setup for Monday has flipped as oil reversed after the domestic close.
items.why: The five-day slide was driven by crude above $100 and Iran-war jitters, but Friday's sharp pullback in oil after Indian hours removed the main pressure point heading into next week.

items.detail: The **retreat in Brent back below $100** is a direct tailwind for India, easing pressure on the country's import bill, trade deficit and inflation and offering support to a rupee that had slid near a record **~96.6 per dollar**.
items.why: As a major net oil importer, India benefits mechanically from cheaper crude, which lowers the current-account and fiscal strain that the earlier spike had intensified.

items.detail: **Foreign institutional investors stayed net sellers**, offloading roughly **₹3,000 crore** of Indian equities and keeping the outflow pressure that has weighed on the market all week.
items.why: Elevated U.S. yields and the oil-driven risk-off mood kept foreign money rotating out of emerging-market equities.

items.detail: With the oil overhang lifting, **Q1 FY27 earnings become the key driver** next week, with banking, IT, auto, FMCG and pharma results in focus after resilient prints from names like Bajaj Auto, TVS Motor and Nestle India.
items.why: A stronger-than-feared earnings season is expected to steer stock- and sector-specific moves once the macro cloud of crude prices clears.

items.detail: **Bitcoin broke below its recent floor to ~$64,030**, down ~1.3% on the day and slipping under the $65K–$66K range it had held all week, pulling the total crypto market cap down ~1.1% to about $2.28 trillion.
items.why: Bitcoin tracked the equity risk-off tone and Middle East uncertainty as institutional buyers paused accumulation.

items.detail: Spot Bitcoin ETFs snapped their seven-day inflow streak with **$225M of net outflows** — the first negative session since July 13 — led by **$202M leaving BlackRock's IBIT**.
items.why: Institutions pulled back amid the equity selloff and Middle East escalation, reversing the steady demand that had cushioned prices earlier in the week.

items.detail: Ether bucked the trend on flows, with **spot ETH ETFs adding $26.3M for a fifth straight inflow day**, even as **ETH slipped to ~$1,857** and **Solana fell ~2.2% to ~$73.97**, dropping back below the $80 level it held earlier.
items.why: Persistent ETF demand kept a bid under Ether products, but spot prices for ETH and SOL still gave ground to the broader risk-off move.

items.detail: Sentiment cooled further as the **Crypto Fear & Greed Index fell 3 points to 28**, holding in 'fear' territory.
items.why: Traders turned cautious as the equity selloff, ETF outflows and geopolitical tension reinforced a risk-reduction theme across markets.

items.detail: Regulatory hopes remain the bull case: the **CLARITY Act has advanced to the full Senate floor** with an **August 10 final deadline** before the Senate's state work period.
items.why: A defined legislative timeline keeps alive the prospect of clearer SEC/CFTC rules that analysts see as a major institutional catalyst if the bill passes.

crossCuttingTheme: The dominant new thread is oil's reversal: Brent dropping back below $100 on hopes for revived U.S.–Iran talks unwound the exact driver behind the prior day's rout — pulling Treasury yields off their highs, letting the S&P 500 and Dow stabilize, and setting up relief for oil-import-heavy Indian equities — even as residual risk aversion still hit chipmakers, sank Bitcoin below $64K and snapped the spot-BTC-ETF inflow streak.
